mechanism.plausibility_rationale: NSAIDs are well-established to cause gastrointestinal hemorrhage due to the inhibition of COX-1, which reduces the production of protective prostaglandins in the gastric mucosa, leading to mucosal injury, ulceration, and subsequent bleeding.
